questions.question: A driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Slowly pass the vehicle at 10 mph or slower.
Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.
Change lanes, look carefully, and pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.
questions.explanation: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. Pedestrians may be crossing that you cannot see. Stop your vehicle and wait until all pedestrians have finished crossing.

questions.question: When you see a person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person is completely out of your way.
Honk your horn as you pass them.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is completely out of your way.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog crossing the street, you must stop. Let them cross completely before you drive. Always give blind pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: Which vehicle must always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: Tank trucks carrying hazardous materials.
Motor homes or pickup trucks towing a boat trailer.
Sport utility vehicles carrying four or more people.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tank trucks carrying hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: A diamond-shaped sign on a truck means the cargo is dangerous (gas, explosives, etc.). These vehicles must stop before crossing railroad tracks.

questions.question: You must give the right-of-way to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street.
At all times.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes must have the right-of-way at all times.

questions.question: You see a pedestrian crossing your lane with no crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact and then pass the pedestrian.
Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must give pedestrians the right-of-way, whether or not there is a marked crosswalk. Stop and let the pedestrian cross safely.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce road rage?

options.text: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes.
Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Use your horn often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, follow all traffic laws and signals. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol from your system?

options.text: Breathe in fresh air.
Let time pass.
Drink coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let time pass.
questions.explanation: Time is the only way to lower your blood alcohol level. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not reduce alcohol in your system.

questions.question: Use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days to:

options.text: Keep your engine warm.
Make your vehicle easier for others to see.
Warn others of bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make your vehicle easier for others to see.
questions.explanation: Use headlights in bad weather so other drivers can see your vehicle. If you need to use your windshield wipers, you must also turn on your low beam headlights.

questions.question: You may pass a vehicle when:

options.text: You are on a hill or curve.
You are on a road with a solid yellow line next to your lane.
You are on a road with a broken yellow line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a road with a broken yellow line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. Only pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: At a crosswalk:

options.text: You must give the right-of-way to pedestrians.
Pedestrians must give the right-of-way to you.
Construction workers must give the right-of-way to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must give the right-of-way to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crosswalks. You must stop for pedestrians in marked or unmarked crosswalks.

questions.question: To prevent yourself from becoming an aggressive driver:

options.text: Stay calm and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the posted speed limit.
Follow the car in front of you closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Focus on driving and do not take other drivers' actions personally. Drive within speed limits and be patient with other drivers.

questions.question: You want to turn right at a corner. A pedestrian with a guide dog is ready to cross in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your engine until the person crosses.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross.
Wait until the person crosses the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the person crosses the street.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes must have the right-of-way at all times. Wait for them to cross completely before turning.

questions.question: Adjust your rearview and side mirrors:

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors, seat, and safety belt before you drive. Do not adjust mirrors while driving.

questions.question: A distraction while driving is:

options.text: Anything that makes you swerve.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can cause crashes, injuries, and deaths.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt, you should:

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Wear both the lap and shoulder belts. Using only one part does not protect you well. If you have an automatic shoulder belt, also fasten your lap belt.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield sign ahead.
Side road entering from left.
Stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a yield sign is coming. Start slowing down when you see this sign.

questions.question: If you experience a tire blowout:

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, take your foot off the accelerator to slow down gradually. Wait until the vehicle has slowed a lot before using the brakes.

questions.question: If you are driving and you see animals standing near the roadway:

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful when you see animals near the road. They may suddenly move or change direction. More animals may be nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: When can you drive in a bike lane?

options.text: During rush hour traffic if there are no bicyclists in the bike lane.
When you are within 200 feet of a cross street where you plan to turn right.
When you want to pass a driver ahead of you who is turning right.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are within 200 feet of a cross street where you plan to turn right.
questions.explanation: You may drive in a bike lane only within 200 feet before making a right turn. Watch for bicyclists or motorcyclists between your vehicle and the curb.

questions.question: If you are riding in a vehicle equipped with a lap belt and a separate shoulder belt, you are:

options.text: Only required to use the lap belt.
Required to use both the lap and shoulder belts.
Only required to use the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required to use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: You must use both the lap belt and shoulder belt when your vehicle has both.

questions.question: When can you drive in a bike lane?

options.text: 30 minutes after sunset or 30 minutes before sunrise
On foggy days when visibility is low
200 feet before making a turn

questions.correctAnswerText: 200 feet before making a turn
questions.explanation: You may drive in a bike lane only 200 feet before making a right turn at a corner or driveway. Do not drive in the bike lane at any other time.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Signal before going any further.
Slow down and yield to trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to trains.
questions.explanation: This round sign means a railroad crossing is ahead. It is posted a few hundred feet before the tracks. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection:

options.text: You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.
You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, always let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first. Turn only when the intersection is clear and the signal allows it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad ahead.
No passing zone.
School zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad ahead.
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign means a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: To pass on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Judge the distance to any oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judge the distance to any oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: It can be hard to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are moving. They may be going faster than they appear. Always make sure you can safely change lanes before passing. If you are unsure about an oncoming vehicle's speed, wait to pass until it has gone by and you have plenty of room to change lanes safely.

questions.question: A steady green traffic light at an intersection means:

options.text: Increase your speed.
Adjust your mirrors.
You may continue through the intersection at a safe and reasonable speed, if it is clear to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may continue through the intersection at a safe and reasonable speed, if it is clear to do so.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can go through the intersection. Let any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection pass first. Then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: If you come to a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing warning lights, you should:

options.text: Drive around the crossing gates if you can't see a train.
Come to a complete stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, and proceed once the gates are lifted.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, and proceed once the gates are lifted.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at a railroad crossing when gates are down or warning devices alert you to a train. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: What is the only effective way to remove alcohol from the body?

options.text: Drink strong coffee.
Wait.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: Time is the only way to remove alcohol from your body. Coffee, food, or cold showers will not help.

questions.question: All of the following are dangerous to do while driving. Which is also illegal?

options.text: Wearing a headset that covers both ears.
Having one or more interior lights on.
Using cruise control on residential streets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a headset that covers both ears.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to wear a headset or earplugs in both ears while driving.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a safe driving practice when driving on the interstate?

options.text: Slower traffic must keep to the right.
Change lanes without signaling.
If you miss your exit, you must go to the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes without signaling.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes. Keep right if you are going slower than other traffic. You cannot back up or make a U-turn on the interstate, so go to the next exit if you miss yours.
